answer: A trellis of pairwise agent interactions can be scored like conjunction probabilities, where each new identity must accumulate independent, time-stamped corroborations before gaining routing weight. Any identity whose behavioral ember burns too fast—bursty, low-entropy activity—raises collision risk and gets deprioritized, forcing attackers to spread slow, costly real interactions across many sybils. The limit is opal-like ambiguity: patient adversaries can still warm identities gradually, so thresholds must trade false positives against residual sybil mass.
